### Data

```{r}
library(lme4)
head(sleepstudy)
tail(sleepstudy)
```

### Example Nr. 1

- For each subject (person) one intercept is added by specifying (1 | subject)

```{r}
m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (1 | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
summary(m)
model_latex <- equatiomatic::extract_eq(m)
knitr::asis_output(paste0( "$$", model_latex, "$$"))
```

### Example Nr. 2

- For each subject one intercept and a own slope is used by specifying (Days | Subject)

```{r}
m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
model_latex <- equatiomatic::extract_eq(m)
knitr::asis_output(paste0( "$$", model_latex, "$$"))
summary(m)
```

### Normales lm

$y = X\beta + \epsilon$

where:

$\beta =
\begin{pmatrix}
  \beta_0 \\
  \beta_1
\end{pmatrix}
$

### linear mixed model

$y = X\beta + Zb + \epsilon$

where:

- the matrix Z decodes:
  * which observation belongs to which subject
  * which slopes belong to which subject
- the vector b contains the estimated parameters:
  * the random intercepts
  * the random slopes
  * $b = (b_{01}, b_{11}, b_{02}, b_{12}, ...)^T$


### Considering the second example

$\begin{pmatrix}
  b_{0j} \\
  b_{1j}
\end{pmatrix} \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)$

where:

$\Sigma = \begin{pmatrix}
  \sigma_0^2 && \rho\sigma_0\sigma_1 \\
  \rho\sigma_0\sigma_1 && \sigma_1^2
\end{pmatrix}$


For the model

```{r}
m <- lmer(Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = sleepstudy)
```

the estimated model can be written as

$$
\text{Reaction}_{ij}
=
(251.4 + b_{0j})
+
(10.47 + b_{1j}) \cdot \text{Days}_{ij}
+
\varepsilon_{ij}
$$

where

$$
b_{0j} \sim N(0, 24.74^2)
$$

and

$$
b_{1j} \sim N(0, 5.92^2)
$$

This means:
- the global intercept is approximately \(251.4\)
- each subject receives an additional intercept offset with a standard deviation of approximately \(24.7\)
- the global slope for `Days` is approximately \(10.47\)
- each subject receives an additional slope offset with a standard deviation of approximately \(5.9\)

An example subject could therefore have the model

$$
(251.4 + 20) + (10.47 - 3)\cdot \text{Days}
$$

The estimated correlation between the random intercepts
and random slopes is approximately \(0.07\),
indicating almost no relationship between both effects.


### Visualization

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(sleepstudy,
       aes(Days, Reaction, group = Subject)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red")
```

### Assumptions

```{r}
m <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject),
  data = sleepstudy
)
qqnorm(residuals(m))
qqline(residuals(m))

library(ggplot2)
df_plot <- data.frame(
  fitted = fitted(m),
  residuals = resid(m)
)
ggplot(df_plot, aes(fitted, residuals)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2)
```

### Inference

```{r}
m <- lmerTest::lmer(
  Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject),
  data = sleepstudy
)
summary(m)
anova(m)
```
